place: A village shop row on delivery morning: one unbroken terrace of small businesses down the near side of the street, the colliery gates and winding gear closing the top of the road, delivery lorries nosed into the kerb with their tailgates down, crates stacked out on the flags outside every doorway.
activity: Everyone is taking in the morning delivery — lifting crates down off the lorries at the kerb, wheeling sack-trucks in through the doorways, signing the docket on the driver's board, and carrying the empties back out to be loaded up again.
anchor_structure: The unbroken run of shopfront fascias with the kerb and gutter line beneath them, running from the lower left of the frame up to the colliery gates at the top right, splitting the picture into pavement, roadway, shopfronts and the upper windows above them.
pun_explanation: A neurotransmitter is a chemical messenger, and Messenger Row is an ordinary street nameplate that carries one morpheme of the everyday referent without printing the medical word — the same device the accepted transmitter reading used, and within the Lithium Lift precedent. This is the one chapter the spec says must not invent a venue: the seven course-wide premises are the content, so the plate is the street they stand on. A shop row is the only mundane container that holds a colliery, a hotel, a dairy, a club door, a weaving workshop, a seed merchant and a police box in one coherent frame at one light source. The delivery round then supplies the whole mechanism free: release is a crate carried in off the lorry, and reuptake is the same hand carrying the empties back out to be loaded again, which is a native action in the trade rather than a metaphor. Each premises signs for its own crate, so every messenger stays addressable at its own doorway instead of becoming one of seven nameplated boxes in a line-up.

The hall was chosen because serotonin's whole story is one narrow midline workshop that ships everywhere, and a market's central aisle is literally its seam: the weaving stall stands on it and its goods go out to every other counter in the building. pun_explanation: Nor'east is the compass reading NE spoken aloud and it is a perfectly ordinary way to name a family show — the corpus already owns the N-compass as the fixed glyph for this transmitter, so the fascia hooks straight onto a symbol the learner already holds. The showground was picked because it is the only mundane workplace that legitimately holds all three fixed structures at once in one light: a band on its own rostrum at the ring fence, a call box at the gate through which every message for the ground passes, and a snowy pine treeline with a pack standing out on the open ground beyond the ropes. It is a morning of work, not a performance, so the register stays flat and the strangeness sits in the props. The trade also pays out on the chapter's own mechanism without invention — everything on the ground is either hauled out on a rope or hauled back in on one, and one keeper stands at the fence with a dart rifle.

The trade was chosen because the coin machine is the only ordinary object whose working parts are a paid-for reward loop, which lets the fixed colliery token stand inside the venue as a genuine period fixture — a penny-in-the-slot working model with a coin slot at the front and a payout cup underneath — instead of being pasted onto a shop that has no room for it. pun_explanation: Tongue and cheek are two genuine butcher's cuts and a name real butchers actually trade under, so the fascia is invisible as a joke, and the organ of speech is sitting literally on the counter in a trade that has nothing to do with speech — the boring container the rules demand, with the anomaly in the props. The shop's own routine then delivers all four subtypes as literal depiction rather than as one subtype printed verbatim. Naming a cut across the glass is the whole transaction, so the customer handed the wrong thing after asking for it, and the customer whose word comes out with the wrong sounds, are both ordinary counter business. A take-a-ticket queue makes turn-taking the venue's own posted rule, which is what the social subtype fails at, and the shop's own machines block, judder and repeat as a matter of course. The wall mirror behind the counter is already there for the therapist's move.

place: A candle works on a bright weekday: a masonry bench of sunken wax melt pots, an overhead dipping rail carrying wick frames the length of the room, a cooling and trimming bench along the window wall, a mould rack in the corner, and a small shop counter with boxed stock at the front.

anchor_structure: The overhead dipping rail — a steel rail hung with rows of wick frames running from the lower left to the upper right above the sunken melt pots — dividing the works into the melt bench, the dipping run, the cooling and trimming bench and the shop counter.
pun_explanation: Dysthymia gives THYME, thyme is said time, and Thyme & Again is a stock real-world shop name that also says time and again — which is the one thing all three of this chapter's disorders have in common: the same mood, sorted only by its temporal shape. The critic accepted that name; what changes is the trade, because the garden centre it stood in belongs to another chapter. A herb-scented candle works keeps the name plausible and buys a far better inventory, because every object in a candle works is a duration or a cycle stated in the trade's own printed units. Boxed stock carries burn times on the lid, which is a native duration carrier with no competing meaning. A taper only exists because the same frame was dipped again and again over hours, one thin layer at a time — persistence is the manufacturing process, not a picture of a mood. The marked calendar candle in its glass case, ringed and burning down through the rings with everything happening in the last few before it goes out, is a genuine historical object and is PMDD's luteal week drawn without a metaphor and without the corpus-luteum detour the critic struck out. The standing-order book on the counter carries monthly deliveries and a two-year run. Inter-episode mood and outbursts are carried by people visibly behaving that way at the trimming bench — literal depiction, the corpus's largest mechanism — not by anything the flames are doing.

Episode type is carried by which tank a can is in — the same can goes into the brine tank and comes out through the thaw tank, one object with two extremes, which is what bipolar means and is why the sign only has to spell half of it.
